claim: The Abvigen AFR-0500-COOH particles are spherical polystyrene, surface-functionalised with carboxyl (-COOH) groups, supplied as a suspension in deionised water.

identifiers.applies_to: the type AFR-0500-COOH. Applying it to the bottle on this bench goes through the E5 linking claim in the sample table

validity_conditions: Applies to the product family as supplied, at every diameter it is sold in, and says nothing about which diameter is in use here (gap tracer_diameter_unknown). WHY THIS IS AN ENTRY AND NOT FILING. Spherical and polystyrene are the two premises a Stokes-Einstein estimate rests on, and a caller that assumes them without a source has made an assumption it cannot cite; carboxyl surface is what governs whether the particles stick to glass or to each other, which is an imaging outcome and not chemistry trivia. THE REFRACTIVE INDEX IS NOT HERE. Polystyrene has a well-known one and this document does not print it, so nothing is entered for it from this source -- but the gap changes character: refractive_index was `absent` and is now findable, because the material is established and a real optical reference can be cited against it. Filling it from memory would be E6 and would enter nothing. NO SUBJECT, AND THAT IS THE HONEST STATE. Check 44 resolves a `quantity` subject against the names actually used in numbers[] somewhere, and refused an earlier draft of this entry with the right instruction attached -- a subject names a registry so that it can be wrong, do not add the id to make this pass. There is no registry id for the tracer particle: `device` is drawn from the channels and elements of kb/staging/devices.v0.json and a sample is not hardware, `configuration` is an optical path, and contracts/observables.json holds two ids, neither of them this. So the field is left off rather than filled with something adjacent. This is the third instance of one structural gap, after `at` having nowhere to point for 'the room' (lab_ambient_temperature) and the per-lens handle in the pixel-size calibrations; it is raised with manager-librarian, who owns contracts/observables.json. 015 WAS WITHDRAWN THE SAME DAY IT WAS ISSUED, AND THIS ENTRY IS ABOUT THE TYPE. For a few hours this entry read that the product identification had been withdrawn and that it was not about the bottle on this bench. The person reversed that on 2026-09-19 after the prior project's records were opened: the bottle IS AFR-0500-COOH, and what is wrong is Abvigen's published data. WHAT DECIDED IT WAS AN ASYMMETRY, NOT A MEASUREMENT, and that is worth keeping because the measurement alone did not settle it. Both explanations -- wrong bottle, or wrong data sheet -- predict green-excited particles visible at 605, and 015's own evidence, a label that says nothing, is equally consistent with either. What broke the tie is that the Abvigen page has two documented errors unrelated to any of this (a monoclonal-antibody filing, and the product name printed in the Particle Size field), so `the data sheet is wrong` is far the cheaper explanation. See abvigen_published_data_is_unreliable. AND THE ENTRY IS STILL NOT DIRECTLY ABOUT THE BOTTLE. Under the instance/type split architecture ruled in 6eaee1b, this is a fact about the TYPE `AFR-0500-COOH`, at E3, from the supplier. The bottle is an INSTANCE and lives in the sample table. The claim joining them -- `this bottle is that product` -- carries its own grade and is E5, because the label is still silent and the person's judgement is what stands in for it; it becomes E3 the day somebody reads a label that says. So applying anything here to the particles on the bench inherits E5 by 5.8, worst in the chain. Restored, but not restored to E3. THE `abvigen_` HANDLES STAY, and they are now right for a different reason than the one they were changed for. They were renamed from `tracer_` because the word `tracer` asserted these were ours in a string nothing checks; they keep the name because these are type-level facts and the type is what they should be named for. A query for our tracer should not land here. THE CLAIM SENTENCE WAS CORRECTED TOO, AND IT HAD BEEN THE LAST PLACE THE OLD ASSERTION SURVIVED. The handles were renamed to `abvigen_` hours earlier, and the first words of the claim still read `The tracer particles...` -- so this entry's body said `a query for our tracer should not land here` while its own headline sentence said these were our tracers. Found by librarian-agent-a5 verifying my report against the tree, which is exactly why that verification was handed over: my account came from memory of what I had done. The entry_id still begins `tracer_` and stays that way deliberately -- it is the citation handle, the polystyrene dispersion entries reference it by name, and renaming it is a deletion under rule 8.
